member.name: T:VideoForensics.Core.Api.Contracts.AuthResultDto
member.summary: Response DTO representing the result of an authentication attempt. Mirrors the server-side record and adds HTTP-serializable fields for handling two-factor authentication flows.
member.param: Indicates whether the authentication attempt succeeded. True if credentials were valid and no further action is required. False if credentials were rejected, or if an error occurred.

Error message providing details if authentication failed. Null when is true or when the only issue is that two-factor authentication is required. Set to a provider-specific error message when credentials are invalid or an error condition occurs.

Authentication token issued by the provider upon successful authentication. Null if is false or authentication is not yet complete (two-factor required). When present, this token can be used for subsequent API requests to the provider.
Expiration time of the authentication token, in UTC. Null if is null. When set, callers should refresh the authentication before this time if token refresh is supported.

The persisted provider account identifier that this login resolved to. Null if is false, if the provider implementation does not persist accounts, or if authentication is incomplete (two-factor required). Callers that attach downloaded devices to an account should use this value after a successful login.

Indicates whether two-factor authentication is required to complete the login. True when the provider rejected the initial username/password and requires a second step with a time-sensitive code. False otherwise (including both success and one-step authentication failures). When true, the client should extract , collect the two-factor code from the user, and issue a second request with .

Short-lived attempt identifier for two-factor authentication follow-up. Non-null only when is true; null otherwise. When set, this identifier uniquely ties the two-factor request back to this authentication attempt, allowing the server to validate that the 2FA code is being submitted for the correct login session.

member.name: T:VideoForensics.Core.Api.Contracts.UpsertJammingIncidentRequest
member.summary: Request body to record (insert or update) a jamming incident. Deliberately carries no CaseId or DetectedAtUtc: those are server-controlled so a client cannot forge a case link or rewrite when an incident was detected. Source is the one client-claimed provenance field (the write route is Admin-only): it lets a client host that ran the analysis itself record incidents as AutoDetected so re-runs dedupe; it applies to NEW incidents only.
member.param: Incident id; (or an unknown id) records a new incident.
The device the incident was observed on.
When the interference began, in UTC. Must be before .
When the interference ended, in UTC.
Number of events affected (non-negative).
Average signal degradation in dB (non-negative).
Confidence level name (Low, Medium, High, Definite).
Optional free-text notes (max 2000 characters).
Optional origin name (AutoDetected or ManuallyRecorded, case-insensitive); null means ManuallyRecorded. Applied to new incidents only; an existing incident keeps its stored source.

member.name: T:VideoForensics.Core.Api.Contracts.LockoutPolicySettingsDto
member.summary: Data transfer object for lockout policy settings: maximum failed login attempts, lockout duration, GeoIP-based country blocking, and lookup failure behavior.
member.param: Maximum number of consecutive failed login attempts before account lockout is triggered.
Duration in minutes that an account remains locked after exceeding MaxFailedAttempts.
Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to block from login (e.g. "KP,IR"). Null or empty means no country-based blocking is enforced.
When true, fail closed (block login) if a GeoIP or threat-intelligence lookup fails. When false, fail open (allow login) on lookup failure.
Timestamp of the last update to these settings, in UTC.
When true, client IPs that trigger lockouts across enough distinct accounts are automatically banned.
Distinct locked-out accounts from one client IP that trigger an auto-ban. Must be at least 1.
Window in minutes over which distinct-account lockouts are counted. Must be at least 1.
Duration in minutes of an auto-created IP ban. Must be at least 1.

member.name: T:VideoForensics.Core.Api.Contracts.SecurityEventDto
member.summary: Data transfer object for a security event (login attempt, breach, lockout, etc.).
member.param: Unique identifier for the event.
The operator whose account this event relates to; null for a failed login whose username matches no operator.
Type of security event (e.g. LoginAttemptFailure, LoginAttemptSuccess, BreachDetected).
Whether the event outcome was successful or failed.
Client IP address where the event originated, if available.
Timestamp of when the event occurred, in UTC.
